To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the EXCESS query language can be extended with versioning constructs that support the following features: (1) versioning at the conceptual level, (2) versioning at a higher level than the database level, and (3) versioning in a multidimensional space.

the EXTRA data model, with its support for versioning, is more powerful than the relational data model, and that versioning can be integrated with the EXCESS data model, which is based on the relational model, without loss of power or expressibility.

versioning and configuration management can be supported in an object-oriented database system by providing a set of primitives to manipulate version sets and by allowing users to specify configurations non-procedurally.
In summary, our research is concerned with
providing the database user with a higher-level interface to versioning and configuration management.
the design of data models that are more flexible, expressive, and user-oriented.
providing a conceptual framework for the management of multiple versions in database systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the versioning and configuration management facilities of the EXCESS system are a major step forward in the development of object-oriented database systems.
the proposed model is a good basis for the implementation of a versioning system that can be easily used by the end user.
the EXTRA data model is a powerful, general-purpose, object-oriented data model that is well suited to the needs of a wide range of applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have extended EXTRA to include the following features: (1) Versioning and configuration management, and (2) A new type of data object, called a version set.
versioning and configuration management are best handled at a high level in the data model, and not at a lower level in the query language.
the EXTRA data model provides the necessary foundation for a new generation of object-oriented data management systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a higher-level versioning model can be supported by a simple object-oriented database system.
the design of a versioning system should not be left to the database designer; rather, the database designer should provide a high-level interface for specifying versioning policies.
the versioning problem can be addressed at a much higher level than has previously been possible.
